First release: the official Seafile server as one container you can install from a template, on Seafile 14.0.8. Upstream still labels Seafile 14 as testing and it cannot be downgraded, so back up the data folder and the database before every update.

## ✨ Added

- The official `seafileltd/seafile-mc` image, with its own scripts still in charge of setting up, starting and upgrading Seafile. On its own it expects MariaDB, Redis and the notification server as separate containers on a shared network, plus a JWT key made by hand.
- The JWT key, the database password and, if the field is empty, the admin password are generated on the first start and kept in `secrets.env` in the data folder. A value set in the template always wins, and the log names a generated admin password once.
- `BUILTIN_MARIADB=true` runs MariaDB 10.11 inside the container, with its data in `/shared/mariadb`, listening only on `127.0.0.1`. An interrupted first start leaves no half-made database behind.
- `BUILTIN_REDIS=true` runs Redis inside the container as a pure cache, with nothing written to disk.
- `ENABLE_NOTIFICATION_SERVER=true` starts the notification server in the same container under `/notification`, so the clients see changes when they happen.
- External MariaDB and Redis stay the default. The root password is used once to create the databases, and with `USE_EXISTING_DB=1` and databases you made yourself it is not needed at all.
- A missing server hostname, database host or Redis host stops the start with one line that says what to set, instead of a Seafile that shows "Page unavailable".
- On shutdown, Seafile stops before the built-in MariaDB and Redis.
- `/shared` keeps the layout of the official image, so a setup from another Seafile template switches over by pointing at the same folder.
- Seafile's logs in the container log, and a health check on `/api2/ping/`.
- Images for linux/amd64, the only architecture the official image is built for.
- Every build starts the image with all built-in services, signs in, uploads a file, restarts and downloads it again. A client subscribed over WebSocket has to receive the upload from the notification server.
